newsitem.title: USA: Florida seeks to improve Prudential settlement.
newsitem.headline: Florida seeks to improve Prudential settlement.

text.p: Florida's treasurer and insurance commissioner said on Thursday that the settlement of a class action lawsuit alleging life insurance sales fraud by Prudential Insurance Co of America is flawed and that he will seek to improve the terms of the settlement.

"Instead of creating a fair restitution system for victims of outright deception, the proposed settlement would provide a financial windfall to only a small portion of the 1.8 million potential victims of the sales abuse known as churning," Bill Nelson said in a press release.
Churning is a term for the inappropriate replacement of life insurance polices and annuities.

"On behalf of the Florida citizens who were deceived, I intend to take whatever steps are needed to improve upon the proposed settlement, including, if necessary, testifying against it in federal civil court in New York when the presiding judge holds a required fairness hearing," he said.
Nelson said his office will continue to investigate.
